activities.caption: pair each Islamic-art feature with what it does
activities.name: atwIslamicMatch

config.prompt: The negotiated constraint produced supreme alternatives — pair each feature with its work:

pairs.right: the word of God given monumental form
star-and-polygon tessellations built from circle constructions
honeycomb vaulting — 3-D stalactite geometry dissolving the ceiling
a silver sheen fired in reduction — chemistry as luxury
reached Europe through Islamic Spain, with a book revolution attached

config.why: The Dome of the Rock (691–92) announced the vocabulary; the Alhambra perfected it — muqarnas and tilework calibrated to Andalusian light.

activities.anchor: Hindu and Buddhist art encode cosmology in architecture
activities.caption: file the landmarks — cosmos, theology or synthesis?
activities.name: atwTempleBuckets

config.prompt: South and Southeast Asia in three registers — file each landmark:

items.label: Angkor Wat — Mount Meru in five towers and a moat-ocean
Borobudur — a stepped mandala of 2,672 relief panels
Chola bronzes — lost-wax casting, each unique: impermanence embedded
Gandhara — wavy hair and Hellenistic drapery on an Indian doctrine
Mughal ateliers — Persian technique fused with Indian colour under Akbar

config.why: The temple you walk through is the diagram; the destroyed wax original makes each Shiva unique; the Silk Road and the atelier do the fusing — history and scripture sharing a wall.

activities.caption: true or false — the 'failed Masaccio' test
activities.name: atwPerspectiveJudge

statements.s: Song painters observed finely and chose a shifting, layered viewpoint.
statements.why: Planes of distance recede as the scroll unrolls — the work is read as a journey in time, not looked through as a window.

statements.s: Chinese landscape painting never mastered perspective.
statements.why: It chose a different convention — single-point perspective is one tradition's habit, not a law of optics the rest of the world failed to discover.

statements.s: Colophons and seals on a handscroll accumulate like a centuries-long seminar.
statements.why: The 'three perfections' put poetry, calligraphy and painting on one sheet, with commentary accruing for generations.

statements.s: Fan Kuan's Travelers Among Mountains and Streams dates to around 1000.
statements.why: c. 1000 — one of the Song monuments that scale humans to brushstroke dots within the cosmos.

activities.anchor: The ethnocentrism this subject must dismantle has a founding exhibit
activities.caption: rebuild the Ife–Benin story, from Atlantis to restitution
activities.name: atwBeninOrder

config.prompt: Renaissance-grade naturalism met period anthropology — put the story in order:
items: the Ife heads are cast in zinc-brass, contemporary with Giotto (12th–15th c.)
the Benin bronzes document the Edo court's history (13th–19th c.)
Britain's punitive expedition sacks Benin City and disperses thousands of objects (1897)
Frobenius sees the Ife heads and invokes Atlantis (1910)
Germany transfers ownership of over a thousand bronzes to Nigeria (2022)
config.why: The record was always African; the frame was the problem — and 1897's catastrophe is what turned the bronzes into the central case of the repatriation debate.

activities.anchor: raised by some lost non-African civilisation
activities.caption: publish the attribution — Great Zimbabwe, 1905
activities.name: atwZimbabweBranch

config.root: 1905. You are the antiquarian facing Great Zimbabwe's dry-stone walls.

start.text: The walls are monumental. Who built them?

choices.label: A lost non-African civilisation — Phoenicians, or the Queen of Sheba's people
Publish nothing until more evidence arrives

myth.text: Colonial wishful thinking — defended for a century against the evidence. The claim said more about the era's anthropology than about the walls.

shona.text: Archaeology is unambiguous: built by the ancestors of the Shona between the 11th and 15th centuries — and Zimbabwe took its modern name from the site for a reason.

wait.text: Defensible — but the dating evidence was already there to read, and the delay let the myth entrench for a century.

config.why: Attribution is never neutral: who you say built the walls is also who you say can build.

activities.anchor: The pre-contact Americas built monumental traditions
activities.caption: pin the movement on the century line
activities.name: atwPapunyaPlace

config.prompt: Papunya Tula translated Dreaming designs — previously sand and body painting — into acrylic on board. In what year?
config.why: 1971, Central Australia — launching the contemporary Aboriginal art movement, now Australia's most significant visual export: 'non-Western' is a geography, never a tense.
config.context: The Bonampak murals date to c. 790 ce and the Moche portrait vessels to the 1st–8th centuries — monumental traditions the colonial frame long demoted.

activities.anchor: belongs to every trade route it travelled
activities.caption: drag the divider — blue-and-white, made and copied
activities.name: atwPorcelainCompare

config.prompt: One decorative schema, five civilisations — drag between origin and echo:

before.label: Made in China (14th c.)
before.text: Chinese kilns fire cobalt decoration for export markets — the pigment imported from Persia, 'Muhammadan blue'.

after.label: Copied everywhere (1400s–1700s)
after.text: Ottoman Iznik re-interprets the palette on fritware; Safavid Persia copies it; Dutch Delft imitates it in the 1600s; Japan's Arita kilns capture the European market when Ming supply collapses.

config.why: The motif is a shared economy with local accents — the cleanest demonstration in material culture that the global history of art is a network, not a set of columns.
